claims.statement: deepagents-code (dcode) is a prebuilt terminal coding agent that packages the deepagents SDK harness together with a terminal experience, persistence, tools, skills, and optional sandboxed execution, as a reference implementation.

dcode has two runtime halves that run in separate processes: a terminal client that owns presentation and input (interactive or headless output plus approvals), and an agent server that owns the agent runtime and connects the model, tools, memory, skills, and backend.

The Textual client treats server checkpoint and stream totals as authoritative thread cost, may display request-keyed provisional stream cost until a server total settles it, discards totals for inactive threads, and warns once on an authoritative threshold crossing.

When background server startup succeeds, `on_deep_agents_app_server_ready` refreshes the mounted status bar's model from runtime state so a retry after a failed startup does not retain stale model text; missing status-bar or model identity is surfaced by warnings, and missing identity clears the displayed provider, model, and effort.

The normal launcher scaffolds a temporary LangGraph project with a persistent SQLite checkpointer, starts a loopback `langgraph dev` server on an ephemeral port by default, waits for the `agent` graph, returns a workspace-configured `RemoteAgent`, and stops the process if startup or cancellation prevents handoff.

The parent reconstructs typed missing-credential or missing-provider-package startup failures only from allowlisted JSON marker fields emitted by the server; other early-exit output is surfaced as a RuntimeError with a bounded log tail.
Each graph execution request must provide a thread ID and workspace context that validates against the durable binding before the server selects a workspace runtime.

Workspace runtime selection rechecks bound access policy, rejects policy or project-trust drift, but rebuilds rather than refuses when only the full runtime identity changes; runtimes are an LRU cache of at most 32 entries keyed by workspace and runtime fingerprint.
A process-wide sandbox is reserved by the first workspace that claims it, and incompatible LangSmith tracing/redaction settings also prevent workspace sharing in the same server process.

The server exposes launch metadata and thread-fenced model resolution/catalog APIs: thread APIs validate request shape and the workspace binding, resolve in the workspace environment without committing a model switch or inference, and map conflicts, validation errors, and unavailable resources to 409, 422, and 503 respectively.

The built-in server owns `/offload`: it runs a thread operation with stable operation IDs across hook-response rounds, rejects conflicts before commit, limits writes to permitted offload state channels, and offers cancellation that waits for a terminal operation outcome.

`RemoteAgent` separates remote graph streaming and state from session-cost reconciliation; it combines graph checkpoint cost with best-effort separately persisted side-question cost and marks a result cached when graph state is unsettled.

`app.py` imports `_textual_patches` for side effect before an `App` is created; the patch module applies independent, best-effort Textual private-API patches that log a warning and leave stock behavior when an individual import or assignment fails.

The static slash-command registry is the single source for command metadata; queue-bypass sets and autocomplete entries are derived from it, and experimental commands are omitted from autocomplete unless experimental mode is enabled.

Slash completion ranks static or dynamic command entries, displays friendly labels while inserting canonical machine names, and plugin skill completion preserves the full namespaced `/skill:` command even when its popup label is shortened.
Thread-reference completion searches cached local thread metadata and inserts an ID-only `@@(thread:<id>)` token; choosing a reference is distinct from resuming a thread or mutating graph state.

Thread names are validated as printable single-line strings of at most 50 characters and are durably saved in a separate SQLite table while mirrored into the newest checkpoint metadata; cache rows are updated without mutating conversation messages.
The app prevents stale asynchronous thread-name reads from replacing the active name and refreshes open thread selectors and thread-reference completion after a successful rename.

`/threads -r [ID]` resolves an explicit target or prefers the previous thread for an unqualified resume; cross-agent local resume has a separate restart path, while a remote session is instructed to relaunch because it cannot switch its remote server.

Both `dcode` and `deepagents-code` console scripts invoke the lazily exported `deepagents_code:cli_main`; lazy resolution avoids loading main startup machinery when package submodules are imported directly.

`cli_main` fast-paths version output, skips Textual dependency checks for ACP mode, installs POSIX termination handlers for cleanup, and dispatches parsed invocation modes after managed-configuration gating.

dcode's ranked configuration resolver gives managed policy, CLI, retained reload values, environment, user configuration, and typed defaults precedence in that order while retaining provenance and provider health.

Parent and server share `ServerConfig`: the parent serializes launch configuration as `DEEPAGENTS_CODE_SERVER_*` environment variables and the graph reads it from the environment, preventing independent client/server configuration schemas.

`RemoteAgent` wraps LangGraph `RemoteGraph` for HTTP/SSE streaming, normalizes streamed messages for the Textual adapter, and keeps workspace descriptors as transport state while the server validates durable workspace bindings.

The sessions database is `sessions.db` in the default state directory; its checkpoint metadata listing index is a best-effort performance optimization that avoids scanning large state blobs without changing listing correctness.
